newsitem.title: CANADA: Forest to decide on Saxon fate.
newsitem.headline: Forest to decide on Saxon fate.

text.p: Saxon Petroleum Inc's fate rests in the hands of major shareholder Forest Oil Corp, which was expected to either sell its stake in the small Canadian firm or buy out its minority holders, a Saxon executive said on Tuesday.
The process would likely take three to six months, Saxon vice-president of finance Chris Bradley said in a telephone interview. Denver-based Forest controls about 65 percent of Saxon.
"The status quo is going to change. They are either a buyer or a seller," Bradley said.

Saxon said late Monday it set up a special committee of directors to assess the company's assets and look for ways to "maximize shareholder value." Financial advisers were expected to be hired shortly.
At its current stock price, Saxon's market capitalization would be about C$127 million on a fully diluted basis. Saxon also has C$30 million in long-term debt.
Its shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange were trading at 0.82 on Tuesday, down from a year-high of 1.20.
Forest also operates in Canada under its own name after acquiring the assets of ATCOR Resources two years ago.

"From their point of view, this just isn't practical over the long term, having two companies up here and having the problems you typically would have as a U.S. company being a 65-percent owner in a Canadian company," Bradley said.
"How much flexibility they have with us and how they can deal with is is fairly limited."

Saxon, which operates mainly in the Bigoray area of Alberta, located between Edmonton and Drayton Valley, produced an average of 2,342 barrels of oil and gas liquids and 8.6 million cubic feet of natural gas a day in the second quarter. ((Jeffrey Jones, Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
